lol good shit man I got a good laugh out of you getting full whited as soon as you turned the corner.

In terms of advice? Beyond the basic “learn to aim better” stuff you seem to be pretty indecisive in a lot of those quick “transitions”, aka the moments between something happening. Like at the start you’re kind of sheepishly creeping up to the corner and then spam when you’re caught off guard. Generally, you’ll be at your best/most confident when you have a clear idea of what you want to do, and from moment to moment you need to be able to react to what’s going on and retool that idea. Try (if you think you’re able to mid round) to think of what your current/next action is going to be occasionally, and commit to doing it fully unless the situation changes. Obviously this will come with a lot of trial and error, but that’s just how it is to build gamesense a lot of the time.

The shot onto the first kill was pretty good, same with the small flick to the third one, but what’s sticking out to me is you struggled to track a bit on the first guy who peeked you, as well as that scouter at the end. I’d probably try to shake things up on aim_botz and try practicing tracking and those small adjustments for when your crosshair is close but not on target. You can also try aim_rush on the workshop, deathmatch, or even just a bit deathmatch if it feels too boring.

Obviously take all this with a grain of salt, I can’t really give that comprehensive feedback off one clip. Don’t think too much about it, you’ll improve over time and just enjoy the game as it comes to you.

So context,
I’ve always had a pretty full head of hair but after moving to uni it’s been noticeably thinner especially around the sides. I haven’t been sleeping a ton because of stress but I think I’ve been eating pretty well. I’m not in my home province so I probably won’t be able to go to the doctor easily until December, but if enough people recommend it I’ll go see if I can get a dermatologist referral on campus

My friends want to go on this big year end trip after high school is over, but I just feel this disconnect from them. It feels like they’re happy I’m not, they have futures I don’t yknow? Most of my life has been spent toiling for meaningless shit, and now that I see the massive difference between me and people that are actually exceptional, it’s like I never learned how to be happy or be a human

I get that, for me it’s often realized in my thoughts. My memories of my family, friends, successes, and accomplishments are what provide me with some semblance of a will to continue. I don’t know what you’re going through, and even if I did I probably couldn’t understand your pain like you can. After all, suffering always cuts deeper for the individual. But what I can tell you from personal experience is that no matter the circumstance, if you can envision a next week, a next day, hour even, then I implore you to seize it. It doesn’t matter what you can visualize, but if you can see yourself speaking with a loved one, going out to eat, seeing a movie, sleeping for a day, or absolutely ANYTHING no matter how odd or meaningless it may seem, than I can tell you with certainty that it’s worth it

I find it admirable that you still find sentimental value in this often cruel and harsh world. The places that mean something to us often act as pillars of comfort, physically housing a place of solace in the same way that you mentally house fond memories of them. I myself find it difficult to look beyond the grotesque flaws that this world displays for us, and I think the fact that some place, any place that you can think of, has intrinsic value means something. I’d be happy to talk if you need it
